claims.claim: Right now, two things from the Sun's core are reaching the Earth. (Hook; A4: all a viewer who swipes at second two keeps.)
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.05379 (BX-P, full text)
claims.note: MSFC: the core's reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'; neutrinos 'pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun and, with some effort, can be detected here on Earth'. BX-P: they 'travel almost undisturbed from the core of the Sun to the surface of the Earth'. Both arrive continuously. The sentence says 'things from the core', not 'light from the core', and 'the Earth', not 'you', so it holds at night too. Nothing false is left with a viewer who leaves here.

claims.claim: The other left it tens of thousands of years ago, maybe far more.
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin of Light'); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759, doi:10.1086/172103; scanned p. 759 read); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior')
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MS92 abstract: '1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffusion time scale of the present Sun'; the usual 3e3-3e4 yr estimates are 'much too short'. MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Sources disagree (4e4 to 1e6), and the script makes the claim all of them support: at least tens of thousands, 'maybe far more' (A3). What 'left' is the energy (MSFC: 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation ... and by convective fluid flows'). Stix (2003, ~3e7 yr) not opened; nothing spoken rests on it alone.

claims.claim: HYDROGEN → HELIUM; SDO photo of the Sun with a ring marked 'CORE' and the tag 'CORE DRAWN AT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS'
claims.where: on-screen: CORE DRAWN AT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS

claims.note: The ring is drawn at 390 * CORE = 97.5 px on a cutout drawn at w=780, i.e. a quarter of the CUTOUT radius (545 image px). But the cutout circle includes a dark rim: the photographed disc's limb is at ~508 image px (median brightness falls from ~145 at r=505 to ~92 at 510 and ~50 at 520). So the ring sits at 136/508 = 0.27 of the Sun's visible radius, not 1/4 (7% too large), while the tag states 1/4 exactly. MSFC: core is the 'innermost 25%' / 'about 25% of the distance to the surface'. Change needed (either): (a) draw the ring at a quarter of the disc, e.g. radius 390 * (508 / 545) * CORE ≈ 91 px (and move the CORE tag to match), or shrink SUN304's cutout radius to ~508; or (b) relabel 'CORE DRAWN AT ABOUT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS'. HYDROGEN → HELIUM itself is confirmed (MSFC, as claim 7).

claims.claim: In twenty fourteen, Borexino's count matched what the sunlight predicts, to within about ten percent.
claims.source_checked: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature13702 (doi:10.1038/nature13702, abstract and article metadata); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.05379 (BX-P, full text)
claims.note: Date: BX-N datePublished/citation_online_date 2014-08-27, Nature 512, 383-386. BX-P: measured rate 144 ± 13 ± 10 vs expected '131 ± 2 (d·100 t)^-1' from the SSM pp flux; flux '(6.6 ± 0.7) x 10^10 cm^-2 s^-1, consistent with the SSM prediction'. 144/131 = 1.10, 6.6/6.03 = 1.09, and the measurement's own uncertainty is ±11%, so 'matched to within about ten percent' is right. 'What the sunlight predicts': BX-P says the agreement 'justifies the assumption made by the SSM that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated', and BX-N frames the result as accounting for '99 per cent of the power of the Sun, 3.84 x 10^33 ergs per second', i.e. the photon luminosity. Plain-word rendering of an SSM prediction tied to the Sun's light; acceptable under A3.

Bars are proportional (3.6 px per count from one baseline at y=900), so the picture does not exaggerate the gap.
